author: PokemanKidd
what_it_is: All levels on Agent unlocked, Team King of the Hill unlocked, but Meltdown is not beat yet.
format: DexDrive .n64: "123-456-STD" and a 0x1040-byte header (DexPlorer comments), then only the first 1792 bytes (pages 0-6) of a Controller Pak: note NO7E/69 "TWINE" ext A, 2 pages; ID block checksums 0101/FEFD (wrong: 0xFFF2 - sum is FEF1)

verified.converted_with: tools/gamefaqs/n64-dexdrive.py convert 007-the-world-is-not-enough.943.n64 OUT: dexdrive: pak = the 1792 bytes after the 0x1040-byte header, padded with 00 to 32 KiB; ID block checksums 0101/FEFD wrong in every copy, rewritten as 0101/FEF1

converted_standalone.how: the same bytes as the .srm regions, as standalone Mupen64Plus keeps them: <GoodName (32 chars)>-<MD5 8>.eep/.sra/.fla/.mpk in its save folder

verified.script: scripts/n64/007 - The World Is Not Enough.load.txt

script_variants.mupen64plus: scripts/n64/007 - The World Is Not Enough.mupen64plus.load.txt

mupen64plus.detail: Load/Save Menu lists note 1 "TWINE" .A, 2 pages (121 pages free); Load on it: "Game Loaded Successfully". The pak as downloaded (ID checksums 0101/FEFD) gets "Corrupt Controller Pak Detected. Repairing May Cause Saved Data To Be Lost. Attempt To Repair?" (standalone variant script: Down held 2 frames)

note: The file stops after page 6 of the pak; the converter pads it with 00 to 32 KiB. Like every pak DexPlorer formatted here, its ID block's second checksum is FEFD where libultra expects FEF1, and the game reports a corrupt pak; the converter rewrites the two checksums (and nothing else) because none of the four ID copies is valid.
